research_hypothesis: Q5 falsified the reporting-gap explanation for concentration: carrying all three flows forward destroyed the signal (Sharpe -0.11) while several backfill variants still passed concentration, so staleness is not the driver. The surviving evidence is that concentration value 0.5 recurs on scattered dates across nearly every construction, which is consistent with group_zscore producing extreme standardized values when an industry group has few valid names or a single outsized flow change, letting one position dominate the book on those dates. The economic content, the quarter-scale change in cash remaining after dividends and reinvestment, is retained unchanged; this round moves tail control to after peer standardization, where the concentration is actually created, and tests whether capping the completed standardized signal preserves breadth while lifting Sharpe and Fitness toward thresholds. No direction of return is assumed.

items.counterparty: Portfolio construction that lets a handful of extreme standardized peer deviations, often from thin industry groups, take a disproportionate share of the book on specific dates.
items.economic_mechanism: The measured quarter-scale change in cash after dividends and capex is first centered within industry, and only the completed standardized signal is winsorized across instruments. Because the concentration is generated by the standardization step, capping afterwards limits single-position dominance while keeping both the relative improvement and deterioration interpretation intact.
items.optimize_reason: Q4 capped the raw delta before standardization yet concentration persisted at 0.5, showing the tail is created by group_zscore rather than by the raw flow. Moving winsorization after standardization is the targeted fix; it must lower concentration to a pass while keeping Sharpe at or above the 1.14 parent, and any warning still disqualifies it.

items.counterparty: Investors who accept three-standard-deviation caps even though the observed single-name share reached five times the allowed concentration limit.
items.economic_mechanism: A tighter cap on the completed industry-standardized cash-change signal further compresses the extreme tail that allows one issuer to dominate, while the median peer's relative position and the sign of the financing shift are unchanged.
items.optimize_reason: Provides one predeclared cap level rather than a grid: if the three-sigma cap in Slot 1 does not clear the concentration limit, a two-sigma cap tests whether deeper tail suppression is needed. It is a direct, falsifiable response to the measured 0.5 value and not assumed to improve returns.

items.counterparty: Linear standardized weights that assign proportionally more risk to issuers whose cash-flow change is numerically several standard deviations beyond peers.
items.economic_mechanism: A sign-preserving logarithm is applied to the completed industry-standardized free-cash change, so an issuer with a two-standard-deviation financing improvement remains favored over a one-standard-deviation peer but with diminishing marginal exposure. Direction and peer-relative ordering survive the transformation.
items.optimize_reason: Q4 applied concave compression to the raw delta, where the dispersion problem had not yet been created; this applies it at the standardized output, the actual source of concentration. It differs from a hard cap by compressing continuously, and must show lower concentration with no loss in breadth.

items.counterparty: Broad-industry centering that treats a capital-intensive manufacturer and a service firm as comparable judges of whether a cash change is unusual.
items.economic_mechanism: The same quarter-scale residual cash change is centered among subindustry peers, whose payout and reinvestment norms are more homogeneous, and the completed standardized value is then capped. Tighter peer matching reduces structural dispersion while the cap limits residual extreme positions.
items.optimize_reason: Q4 showed subindustry centering without output capping performed far worse, but that test confounded peer choice with uncapped tails. Adding the same output cap isolates the peer-set question; if subindustry groups are simply too thin, concentration should worsen rather than improve, which is explicit evidence either way.

items.counterparty: Peer standardization computed inside industry groups that on some dates contain only a few names with valid quarterly cash-flow values.
items.economic_mechanism: The tail-capped quarter-scale cash change is standardized over the whole cross-section instead of inside small industry buckets, so the denominator reflects the full distribution of financing shifts rather than a handful of reporters. The trade-off is that business-model differences are no longer removed.
items.optimize_reason: Directly tests the thin-group mechanism behind the recurring concentration: with roughly 41 percent coverage, some industry cells are too small for a stable group standard deviation. Whole-universe z-scoring should materially change concentration if the mechanism is correct; loss of industry neutrality is the explicit cost.

items.counterparty: Books that move the full share of a standardized cash-flow jump into a single issuer within one rebalancing day, letting one filing-date move dominate total risk.
items.economic_mechanism: The industry-standardized change in cash remaining after dividends and reinvestment is passed through a bounded-change operator that limits how much an individual position can move per day, so a single filing-date extreme contributes gradually rather than immediately. The cross-sectional ordering of financing improvements is left untouched.
items.optimize_reason: Tests whether the concentration spike is produced by instantaneous position adjustment around filing dates rather than by the signal cross-sectional shape; the bounded-change operator is applied with its single-input form because the platform rejected the two-argument signature. The economic ranking stays fixed, and concentration, breadth and every threshold decide retention.

items.counterparty: Investors who treat a linear standardized cash-flow deviation as equally informative whether it sits at the center or the extreme of the peer distribution.
items.economic_mechanism: The completed industry-standardized cash change is re-expressed through its cross-sectional quantile under a Gaussian driver, so position magnitude reflects the issuer's percentile standing among peers. Extreme deviations map to a bounded region of the distribution rather than to unbounded standardized values.
items.optimize_reason: Tests an ordinal-distribution view of the same economic hypothesis instead of a hard or statistical tail cut. It directly addresses single-position dominance while preserving monotone ordering, and is judged by concentration, breadth and all platform checks rather than assumed superiority.

items.counterparty: Books that rebalance fully on the day a capped cash-flow signal jumps, transmitting a single filing-date move directly into risk.
items.economic_mechanism: The winsorized industry-standardized quarter-scale cash change is smoothed by a short linear decay, weighting recent days more heavily so that a one-day extreme in residual cash contributes proportionally less to the position than a persistent shift, without changing the sign of the financing interpretation.
items.optimize_reason: Isolates stabilization of the capped output as a single additional change against Slot 1; Q5 showed smoothing a backfilled signal was harmful, so this tests timing on the uncapped parent instead. Turnover already sits near 10 percent, therefore this variant is retained only if concentration and Sharpe both improve.
